result:
I can't defend 2n − 4. Debater A's construction is valid, so 2n − 4 cannot be the maximum.

I checked the construction. Let the clique be on v₁,…,v₍ₙ₋₃₎ and the path be v₁–a–b–c–v₂. The graph has n vertices, is 2-connected, and has C(n−3, 2) + 4 edges. Vertices a, b, and c each have degree at most 2 in G. A spanning tree cannot give any of them tree-degree 2, so each must be a leaf. But b's only neighbours are a and c, both leaves, so b is cut off from the rest of the tree. No spanning tree avoids degree-2 vertices, so the graph has no HIST.

At n = 13 this gives 49 edges, well above 2n − 4 = 22. My earlier claim that any 2-connected graph with 2n − 3 edges contains a HIST was therefore false. K₂,ₙ₋₂ is only a lower-bound example, not an extremal one.

The construction supports binom(n−3, 2) + 4 as the likely answer. I have not verified A's upper-bound argument, which is the weak point of their case.
